questions.stem: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 4 and 6 hours respectively. Together, how long will they take?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Combined rate = 1/4+1/6 = 3/12+2/12 = 5/12 per hour. Time = 12/5 = 2.4 hours. Short Trick: (4×6)/(4+6) = 24/10 = 2.4 hours.

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 8 hours and Pipe B empties it in 12 hours. If both are opened together when the tank is empty, how long to fill it?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Net rate = 1/8 − 1/12 = 3/24 − 2/24 = 1/24 per hour. Time = 24 hours. When an outlet pipe is opened with an inlet, the effective rate decreases — always subtract the drain rate.

questions.stem: Two pipes A, B fill a tank in 20 and 30 minutes. A drain pipe C empties it in 15 minutes. With all three open, how many minutes to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Net rate = 1/20 + 1/30 − 1/15 = 3/60 + 2/60 − 4/60 = 1/60 per minute. Time = 60 minutes.

questions.stem: An inlet pipe fills a tank in 6 hours. Due to a leak, the full tank empties in addition — so the tank takes 8 hours to fill. How long will the leak alone take to empty a full tank?
questions.explanation: D is correct. With leak: effective rate = 1/8 per hour. Fill rate = 1/6. Leak rate = 1/6 − 1/8 = 4/24 − 3/24 = 1/24. Leak alone empties in 24 hours.

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 10 hours. After 2 hours, Pipe B is opened and the full tank is filled in 4 more hours. How many hours does B alone take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: C is correct. A fills 2/10 = 1/5 in 2 hours. Remaining = 4/5. In 4 hours (A+B): rate = (4/5)/4 = 1/5 per hour. A's rate = 1/10. B's rate = 1/5−1/10 = 1/10. B alone = 10 hours.

questions.stem: Three taps A, B, C can fill a tank in 12, 18 and 9 hours respectively. They are opened alternately each for 1 hour starting with A. How long does the tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: D is correct. In one 3-hour cycle (A then B then C): 1/12+1/18+1/9 = 3/36+2/36+4/36 = 9/36 = 1/4. In 4 complete cycles = 12 hours, exactly 4×(1/4) = 1 tank. Tank fills exactly at end of 12th hour.

questions.stem: A cistern is 1/4 full. Two pipes A, B can fill it in 14 and 16 hours respectively. How long to fill the remaining 3/4?
Pipes A, B fill a tank in 12 and 15 hours. Pipe C drains it in 20 hours. All are opened at 7 AM. At what time is the tank full?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Net rate = 1/12+1/15−1/20 = 5/60+4/60−3/60 = 6/60 = 1/10 per hour. Time = 10 hours. 7 AM + 10 hours = 5 PM.

questions.stem: A pump fills a tank in 2 hours. Due to a crack, it takes 2 hours 30 minutes. How long will the crack alone take to empty a full tank?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Pump rate = 1/2. With crack: rate = 1/2.5 = 2/5. Crack rate = 1/2−2/5 = 5/10−4/10 = 1/10. Crack alone empties in 10 hours.

questions.stem: A tank is filled by three pipes with flow rates in ratio 1:2:3. The largest pipe alone fills the tank in 3 hours. How long do all three together take?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Let unit rate = r. Largest pipe = 3r, fills in 3 h → 3r × 3 = 1 → r = 1/9 per hour. Total combined rate = (1+2+3)r = 6r = 6/9 = 2/3 per hour. Time = 1/(2/3) = 1.5 hours.
